subject: anaesthesia
title: Postoperative Residual Curarisation: Monitoring, Tetanic Fade, and Safety Standards

steps.title: Postoperative Residual Curarisation (PORC)
steps.tx: **Postoperative residual curarisation definition** describes persistent objective neuromuscular weakness (train-of-four ratio under 0.9) upon arrival in the post-anaesthesia care unit following general anaesthesia. Occurring in up to 30 to 40 percent of patients reversed subjectively without quantitative acceleromyography, PORC represents a major preventable driver of postoperative critical respiratory events, hypoxaemia, and microaspiration.

rows: Obstructive hypopnoea and upper airway collapse

steps.title: Failure of Subjective Clinical Tests
steps.tx: **Unreliability of clinical muscle strength tests** highlights why five-second sustained head lift, forceful hand grip, tongue protrusion, and inspiratory tidal volumes under 500 milliliters fail to exclude residual curarisation. A patient can readily perform a five-second sustained head lift with an objective TOF ratio as low as 0.60 to 0.70, harboring up to 70 percent residual nicotinic receptor occupancy in pharyngeal and respiratory muscles.

right.title: Quantitative Acceleromyography (TOF >0.9)

steps.title: Mechanisms of Tetanic Fade
steps.tx: **Pathophysiology of non-depolarizing tetanic fade** reflects presynaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptor blockade during high-frequency motor stimulation. Sustained 50-Hertz tetanic motor stimulation normally stimulates presynaptic nicotinic receptors on the motor nerve terminal to mobilize vesicle stores, maintaining high acetylcholine release. Non-depolarizing relaxants block these presynaptic receptors, rapidly exhausting vesicular release and generating muscle contraction fade.

steps.title: Train-of-Four Stimulus Characteristics
steps.tx: **Standard train-of-four stimulation parameters** deliver four supramaximal square-wave electrical pulses of 0.2-millisecond duration at a frequency of 2 Hertz (one pulse every 0.5 seconds, total cycle 1.5 seconds) over an accessible peripheral motor nerve. Train-of-four cycles must not be repeated more frequently than every 15 to 20 seconds to prevent post-stimulation exhaustion and false-positive fade.

steps.title: Post-Tetanic Count Deep Monitoring
steps.tx: **Post-tetanic count deep blockade assessment** evaluates intense neuromuscular blockade when all four train-of-four twitches are absent (TOF count of zero). The stimulator delivers a 50-Hertz tetanic stimulus for five seconds (which drives massive calcium entry and mobilizes presynaptic acetylcholine), pauses for three seconds, and then delivers 1-Hertz single twitches. The number of elicited twitches correlates inversely with minutes remaining until first TOF twitch return.

steps.title: Double-Burst Stimulation Tactile Detection
steps.tx: **Double-burst stimulation tactile superiority** overcomes the human tactile threshold that cannot reliably detect train-of-four fade when the TOF ratio surpasses 0.60. Double-burst stimulation delivers two short 50-Hertz tetanic bursts separated by 750 milliseconds (DBS 3,3 consists of three pulses per burst). Tactile fade between the first and second muscle twitch is discernible by manual palpation up to a TOF ratio of 0.80.

steps.title: Acceleromyography and Objective Monitoring
steps.tx: **Quantitative acceleromyography monitoring technology** employs a piezoelectric sensor strapped to the thumb over the adductor pollicis tendon. Based on Newton second law (Force equals mass times acceleration), the transducer measures thumb acceleration upon ulnar nerve stimulation, calculating an objective digital TOF ratio and eliminating human observer error.

steps.title: ASA and ESAIC International Standards
steps.tx: **International neuromuscular safety guidelines** published by the American Society of Anesthesiologists and the European Society of Anaesthesiology mandate quantitative objective neuromuscular monitoring for every patient receiving non-depolarizing relaxants. Extubation is prohibited until acceleromyography confirms a TOF ratio greater than 0.90 at the adductor pollicis, backed by routine pharmacologic reversal with sugammadex or neostigmine.
